top_signals.title: Japan’s Trade Deficit Doubles as Hormuz Crisis Hikes Energy Import Costs
top_signals.summary: Japan booked a trade deficit of $17.8 billion (2.82 trillion Japanese yen) for April to September, almost double the deficit from a year earlier, government data showed on Wednesday, as the Middle East crisis made energy imports into the resource-poor G7 economy much more expensive. Between April and September, the period right after the Iran war began and choked oil and LNG supply at the Strait of Hormuz, the value of Japan’s exports rose by 18.4% while the value of imports jumped by 20.4%, according to the Finance Ministry’s provisional…
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: Tehran is a Different Beast Now
top_signals.summary:
The Tehran that the world knew is gone. It died in the fires with former Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei on the first day of the war in February. His son and new Supreme Leader, Mojtaba Khamenei — wherever he is and in whatever physical condition — witnessed his father, wife, and other close family members die in the same airstrike that wounded him. The White House believed that the conflict would last only a few weeks, but the Islamic Republic has proven less fragile than anticipated by the United States and Israel, who now must deal with surviving Iranian leaders
